title: Member properties on enum members: native in_subset versus a scalar ci:properties annotation
question: Do permissible-value in_subset member properties (ClaimModality premise_forming / attribution_identifying / conflict_bearing, StatementKind claim_bearing, segment-kind annotation_unit / statement_anchor / search_block / container) pass linkml-lint per file with S4's .linkmllint.yaml and read back through SchemaView, and does the scalar ci:properties fallback round-trip?
method: Copies of S4's core.yaml in two forms (in_subset with the eight subsets declared; one scalar ci:properties annotation per member, space-separated) plus a SegmentKind probe enum, and a seeded copy naming an undeclared subset on one member; linkml-lint 1.12.1 per file with S4's lint config; SchemaView 1.12.1 readback of each member's in_subset or annotation compared with an independent hand-written expectation table; yaml_dumper and json_dumper round trips; gen-json-schema and gen-pydantic accept each file.

outputs.role: the probe schema copies and their lint reports
lint summary, readback, accessors, round trips, generators

results.name: in_subset_lint_errors
results.note: 2 warnings, the S4 baseline's own (standard_naming on t and v)

results.name: seeded_undeclared_subset_caught
results.note: no_undeclared_subsets error on the permissible value

results.name: in_subset_membership_equal
results.note: pv.in_subset read back equals the independent table

results.name: ci_properties_membership_equal
results.note: annotation value split on spaces equals the table

results.name: permissible_value_ancestors_exposes_subsets
results.note: returns is_a closure only (['supposed']); not a member-property accessor

results.name: annotation_dict_reaches_members
results.note: annotation_dict takes element names; a permissible value is not one (AttributeError)

conclusion: Native in_subset works for member properties: linkml-lint 1.12.1 lints permissible-value in_subset (no_undeclared_subsets covers enums and their members, an undeclared name is an error), SchemaView returns it as get_enum(E).permissible_values[m].in_subset (also through induced_enum), and the yaml and JSON dumps that feed the revision hash keep it. The scalar ci:properties fallback also round-trips. The plan's named accessors do not apply: permissible_value_ancestors is the member is_a closure and annotation_dict does not address members; the consumer reads pv.in_subset directly. Member-property subsets share the schema's one subset namespace with element subsets (structural, unsupported), so the declaration check must tell them apart. Feeds M1: in_subset is viable as the declaration form.
